title: Zephyrine and the Portrait
premise: Bram Vane returns to the decaying Vane estate to bury her twin sister Zephyrine, only to learn the body in the coffin is not her sister. When an excavation crew unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside, Bram's compulsive documentation begins recording things she never wrote: entries dated after her death, entries in Zephyrine's hand. The house has been keeping count of its residents for generations, and each signing of the inheritance papers adds a name to that ledger. As relatives gather for the reading of the will, Bram realizes the family must leave before the last resident signs—or be absorbed into the portrait that hangs, slowly repainting itself, above the hearth. In the end, Bram burns the ledger and signs nothing, trading her memory of Zephyrine for her siblings' escape, and walks out of the house unable to remember why she came.
about_author: Paloma Almeida is a former archivist from the Azores who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned estates before turning to fiction. Her work explores what documents remember when people cannot.

chapters.title: The Wrong Sibling
chapters.summary: Bram arrives at the Vane estate for Zephyrine's funeral and discovers the casket holds a stranger wearing her sister's face. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; her notebook becomes both comfort and weapon.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dying House
chapters.summary: Bram catalogs the estate room by room, documenting decay and the strange absence of any photograph of Zephyrine past age nine. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: obsessive order as armor against dread.

chapters.title: The Excavation Crew
chapters.summary: Crews begin digging the new drainage line and strike something beneath the east lawn: a stone door, its iron ring fused, sealed from within. POV: Bram and foreman Odile. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding unease.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The door resists every tool until it opens on its own at dusk, exhaling air that smells of fresh ink. Inside: a stairwell lined with ledgers. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: vertigo—the house was never empty.

chapters.title: Ledger One
chapters.summary: Bram reads the oldest ledger: names of residents, dates of arrival, dates of 'completion.' Her grandmother's name appears twice. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: horror of pattern recognition.

chapters.title: Family Arrives
chapters.summary: Relatives gather for the will's reading—uncle Corvin, cousins Maren and Tessin, all strangers shaped like family. Each carries a copy of papers they've been asked to sign 'on arrival.' POV: rotating among the cousins. Emotional beat: performative warmth over buried rivalry.

chapters.title: The Portrait Above the Hearth
chapters.summary: Maren notices the ancestral portrait now shows four figures where there were three—and the newest face resembles Zephyrine. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: denial cracking into fear.

chapters.title: Entries in Another Hand
chapters.summary: Bram finds new pages in her own notebook describing events she hasn't witnessed yet, written in Zephyrine's handwriting. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: terror of being authored by something else.

chapters.title: Corvin Signs Early
chapters.summary: Eager for his share, uncle Corvin signs his papers that night. By morning he is cheerful, compliant, and no longer remembers his daughter's name. POV: Tessin. Emotional beat: greed's price made visible.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Bram cross-references the ledgers: the house counts its residents, and the current tally is one short of some threshold. The final signature completes it. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: What Odile Found Below
chapters.summary: Foreman Odile descends alone and returns mute, sketching the same door endlessly on scrap metal. She quits and begs the family to leave. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: witness guilt; the outsider sees clearest.

chapters.title: Zephyrine's Room, Unchanged
chapters.summary: Bram breaks into the sealed nursery wing and finds Zephyrine's room preserved mid-use: warm tea, wet ink, a window painted shut from inside. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: The lawyer reads the will: the estate passes only to whoever remains resident at month's end. Everyone must stay to inherit; leaving forfeits everything. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: trap sprung—money versus flight.

chapters.title: Tessin Bargains
chapters.summary: Tessin tries to negotiate with the house, offering someone else's signature in exchange for his own freedom. The ledgers accept his terms and add his handwriting to their pages. POV: Tessin. Emotional beat: betrayal as self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Portrait Repaints
chapters.summary: Over three nights the portrait gains two more figures—Corvin and Tessin—each rendered mid-smile, eyes following light sources. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: mourning the already-lost.

chapters.title: Séance of Paper
chapters.summary: Bram attempts contact through the ledgers themselves, writing questions and receiving answers in Zephyrine's hand: 'I am not below. I am the count.' POV: Bram. Emotional beat: hope inverted—her sister may be the house's instrument.

chapters.title: Odile Returns With Fire
chapters.summary: Odile comes back with kerosene and a plan to burn the cellar archive, but fire refuses to catch near the door; the flames bend toward the house instead. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: desperation meeting the limits of force.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Bram realizes the 'last resident' clause means whoever signs final papers becomes the house's keeper forever—Zephyrine signed years ago, which is why she couldn't die. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: devastating clarity about her twin's fate.

chapters.title: Evacuation
chapters.summary: Bram and Maren forge exit papers for the surviving family, but the doors now open onto the same hallway. They escape through the excavation shaft as the house seals behind them. POV: alternating Bram/Maren. Emotional beat: frantic solidarity against closing walls.

chapters.title: The Bargain at the Door
chapters.summary: At the threshold the house offers Bram a trade: her memories of Zephyrine in exchange for unsealing the way out. She signs the burning page with her own hand. POV: Bram. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest signature.

chapters.title: Ash Ledger
chapters.summary: The ledgers ignite at last, the portrait blisters and runs, and the family stands on the lawn watching windows go dark one by one—as if the house were blinking. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: exhausted, incomplete victory.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Months later, Bram fills notebooks with blank pages, unable to recall why she came home or whom she buried. On the final page, unfamiliar handwriting appears: 'Thank you.' POV: Bram. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—an identity saved by forgetting what it cost.
